_readme: GAME CONTENT: how PvE encounters are put together from enemy-library.json. Shapes are generated encounters: the runtime EncounterGenerator picks a variant (by Weight), draws each slot's count in [Min, Max] and each unit's type uniformly from Types, and keeps the draw only if its summed enemy Threat is inside [ThreatMin, ThreatMax], it has at least MinDistinctTypes types and it seats on the arena; units are placed front to back (Vanguard, Skirmisher, Ranged; library order within a stance). Each lineup then draws an element scheme by SchemeWeights (Uniform: one element for the whole team; PerType: one per type; PerUnit: one per unit; None), with elements dealt from a shuffled deck of the ten so every element is dealt before any repeats. Shape ids are drop-tables.json's shape ids (the validator requires the two sets to match): a cleared encounter pays out from its shape's drop cell. Templates are authored fixed encounters ({ EncounterId, DisplayName, Description, ShapeId, Arena, Groups: [{ EnemyId, Count, Elements }], DifficultyOverride }; Elements are cycled over the group, empty = no element; DifficultyOverride 0 = use the shape's calibrated difficulty). None are authored yet: which set pieces the game has is a producer decision. Difficulty: every enemy's HP, Attack, Defense, SpecialAttack and SpecialDefense are multiplied by the shape's calibrated multiplier at the encounter's level (encounter-difficulty.json, written by the balance simulator's --write-difficulty, interpolated between the calibrated levels) times DifficultyScale. PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW: DifficultyScale is 1.0 and the table is calibrated so a player who scouts and counter-picks (the simulator's bond-aware heuristic pick) clears each shape's TargetClear (the tiered targets, a user decision: squad and horde 80%, elite 60%, solo 50%; encounter-difficulty.json records the target of every cell); whether the campaign should be that hard, and how a map node picks a shape and a level, are producer decisions not made here. Validated by EncounterLibraryValidator (the Editor importer Beast Craft/Data/Import Encounters, the EditMode tests, Tooling/BalanceSim): every shape's worst case (each slot at Max, each unit its slot's largest type) and every template must fit its arena's enemy deployment zone. The shapes and weights came over unchanged from the balance simulator's former fixtures; see docs/design/battle-system.md, 'Encounter direction'.

Shapes.Description: One giant: huge HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn and a periodic area slam in both. Compositions differ only in the giant's element.
A boss with an escort: one giant and two standard enemies, or two champions (mini-bosses) and one or two standard enemies.
Four to six standard enemies of at least three types: melee tanks, hunters, archers, casters and shamans.

Sixteen to twenty-four enemies: mostly swarm (tiny melee: swarmlings bite, physical; stinglings sting, special; one skill each, since every hit deals at least the damage floor), with a few archers and casters behind them.
